headline: Teams scramble as FAA ground stop threatens to upend sports calendar
author: Stephanie Apstein, Noah White

paragraphs.text: Five buses carrying almost 200 members of the Washington Huskies football team’s traveling party had just pulled up to King County Airport on Friday night when they got the alert: The FAA had instituted a nationwide ground stop.
The team was headed to East Lansing, Michigan, to play Michigan State at 4:15 p.m. Saturday — until it wasn’t.
The team lingered at the airport for half an hour before deciding to return to campus, where the players milled around Husky Stadium in their team sweatsuits.
“There’s not much we can do until there’s some clarity as to when flights might resume,” assistant athletic director Jeff Bechthold said in an interview. “It’s a 30-hour drive.”

College football teams throughout the country are scrambling to rebook travel or find alternative routes as the nationwide FAA ground stop left them unable to fly to the sites of this weekend’s games, while teams in other leagues wait to see how long the ground stop will last.

The Knoxville News-Sentinel reported that Tennessee, which is scheduled to play Texas A&M in College Station, Texas, at 3 p.m. Saturday, was stuck at the airport, waiting for news on a 4 p.m. Friday flight that never took off. CBS Sports reported that Auburn, which is scheduled to play Mississippi State at noon Saturday in Starkville, Mississippi, was in the same position.

College football teams probably will be most affected by the ground stop, as many schools travel on Fridays for Saturday games. Team planes, which are often school-owned among Power Four programs, follow a strict itinerary, departing from regional airports sometime during the afternoon or evening the day before games, to avoid athletes missing their classes as much as possible. Only in rare instances do schools travel on the day-of for games.

NBA, NHL and college basketball teams could also face scheduling adjustments. Ten NBA teams are on the road Saturday, and a handful are playing Friday night in a different city, as well. After Friday night games, they’d usually fly to their next city on a red-eye rather than waiting until the following morning. NHL teams follow similar scheduling practices.
NFL teams typically fly on Saturdays for Sunday games.

Hope that the FAA full ground stop is quickly and easily fixed and everything's OK soon.Just a detail: The 49ers are scheduled to fly to Dallas tomorrow. They often fly out on Fridays if it's multiple time zones, but not this time.— Tim Kawakami (@timkawakami) November 13, 2026
If the ground stop were to continue into Saturday, NFL teams might consider driving, depending on the proximity of their Sunday opponent.
